name: Apollo 17 rover
intro: This rover carried Gene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt almost 36 km around the Taurus-Littrow valley in December 1972, farther than any other Apollo rover. It still wears a fender repaired with maps and tape, and it is parked where its camera filmed the last Apollo liftoff.
status: Parked forever where it filmed liftoff

hotspots.title: The patched fender
hotspots.text: Cernan accidentally knocked off part of this fender, and the wheel sprayed the crew with dust. Overnight, engineers worked out a fix: a fender made of taped-together maps held on with clamps.

source.label: NASA photo AS17-137-20979: the repaired fender

photo.alt: Close-up of a rover wheel with a makeshift fender made of folded maps held on with clamps.
photo.caption: The repaired fender: stiff maps taped together and clamped on.

hotspots.title: Steering stick
hotspots.text: Cernan drove with this T-shaped stick: push it forward to go, pull it back to brake, and tilt it to steer.

source.label: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

photo.caption: Gene Cernan’s first test drive on 11 December 1972, before loading the rover.

hotspots.title: The batteries
hotspots.text: Two 36-volt batteries powered the rover, and they could not be recharged. When they ran down, the rover went quiet for good.

source.label: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

hotspots.title: The TV camera
hotspots.text: Ed Fendell in Houston steered this camera by remote. On 14 December 1972 he tilted it up at just the right moment to follow Challenger’s cabin into the sky.

source.label: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: Apollo 17 return to orbit

hotspots.title: Wire wheels
hotspots.text: These tyres are woven from steel wire with titanium treads, so they could never go flat.

source.label: NSSDCA: The Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle

funFact: The replacement fender was made from four stiff paper maps, gray tape and two clamps borrowed from inside the lander.
whyLeft: Its batteries could not be recharged, and it had done its job: Cernan parked it east of Challenger so its camera could film the liftoff.
repurpose: It might roll again with new batteries and solar panels, but heritage rules say look, don’t touch. Its patched fender is a lesson in fixing things with whatever you have.
